headline: NQ remains in the CME weekend halt with no live price path: Tail stays low at 9% and EA_ON, while Stress holds elevated at 45% on a closed Strait of Hormuz, a ~5% weekly oil rally, a sharp July retail-sales and sentiment miss and an unprecedented Iran sanctions package flagged for next week.
statusText: CME equity-index futures have been shut since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so there is no observable price path this hour and none anywhere in the 24-hour horizon, which ends at 00:00 UTC on 16 August. Tail is 9% (low), holding the action at EA_ON and the status green: pathological one-way structure cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than any observed extension. Friday's verified close supports that reading - the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13%, mid-range inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 band and about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20, with VIX at 14.25 (-2.60%) after a contained 14.18-14.72 day range. Stress is 45% (elevated) and is deliberately held well above the 9-14% weekend floor used in earlier halt runs, because the volatility backdrop is genuinely unresolved rather than merely dormant: the Strait of Hormuz is in its 167th day of effective closure with roughly one transit on 9 August against about 73 per day normally, WTI settled at $82.40 and Brent at $88.52 after a roughly 5% weekly rally, July retail sales fell 0.6% month-on-month against +0.1% expected, University of Michigan preliminary August sentiment collapsed to 51.0 from 55.2, a 30-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.216% - the highest in 25 years - and semiconductor leadership wobbled with Broadcom down about 6% and Applied Materials off more than 5% despite an above-consensus revenue forecast. Confidence is 56% (medium-low): exact index levels, VIX with its day range, 2Y/10Y yields, oil, H.15 constant maturities and a cross-verified seven-day calendar were all read from primary sources this hour, and last hour's 10-year inconsistency is now resolved, but the single most important input - live price structure - is unobservable for the entire horizon, which caps the reading below the solid band.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (9%) alone. With no venue quoting anywhere in the 24-hour horizon there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window, and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it. The operative checkpoint is the CME Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August, where accumulated weekend headlines would express as an opening gap rather than as intraday structure; the danger window brackets that reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery. The gap risk is genuinely two-way: Treasury Secretary Bessent has flagged an unprecedented Iran economic-isolation package for next week alongside continued blockade enforcement, while Iran ties any Hormuz reopening to an end to that blockade and to sanctions relief - either thread can move oil and risk appetite over the weekend. Do not assume continuity with Friday's calm close through that gap; re-score on observed evidence once price discovery resumes. The next scheduled macro checkpoint is FOMC Minutes on 19 August at 18:00 UTC. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout. This is a general market assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and it is not a recommendation to place any trade.
body:
No live price path is available this hour. CME equity-index futures closed for the weekend at Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so directional efficiency, pullback depth, repeated extension and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable for the whole of the current 24-hour horizon. Everything below is the last confirmed state plus corroborated news, and that limitation - not a judgement that markets are calm - is what caps Confidence below the solid band.

Last confirmed structure (Friday 14 August U.S. cash session): the Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13%, against a 30,084.50 previous close, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 session range and roughly 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20 (52-week range 22,841.42-30,762.20). Closing mid-range rather than pinned at an extreme is the single most important structural fact available, and it argues directly against pathological one-way structure. The S&P 500 closed at 7,785.76 (-13.23, -0.17%), the Nasdaq Composite at 26,729.16 (-73.86, -0.28%) and the Dow at 53,732.41 (-107.58, -0.20%), all slipping from Thursday's record close while still capping a third consecutive weekly gain. Breadth actively contradicts a large-cap breakdown: the Russell 2000 rose 0.51% to 3,068.42 and notched a fresh record while the megacap indices fell, so Friday was rotation rather than de-risking. VIX closed at 14.25, down 0.38 or 2.60% from 14.63, having traded only 14.18-14.72 - a level and a range entirely inconsistent with a stressed or one-way tape.

Macro was the drag, and it was a genuine miss on both prints: July retail sales fell 0.6% month-on-month against +0.1% consensus, the largest decline since May 2025, with the control group at -0.4% against +0.3% expected; the University of Michigan preliminary August sentiment index printed 51.0 against 55.2 prior and a 54.5-54.6 consensus. Company-level pressure was concentrated rather than broad: Broadcom fell about 6%, Applied Materials fell more than 5% despite guiding revenue above estimates, and Nvidia was effectively unchanged at 225.16 (-0.14). Energy and basic materials outperformed while technology weighed, in what the tape was described as low-volume summer trading.

Cross-asset: WTI settled at $82.40 (+$1.15, +1.42%) and Brent at $88.52 (+$1.45, +1.67%), extending a roughly 5% weekly gain and a 32-34% year-on-year rise, on the U.S. tightening economic pressure on Iran to reopen Hormuz and an IEA warning of deepening supply deficits. On rates, last hour's inconsistency is now resolved from session reporting: the 10-year closed near 4.67% (+5bp) and the 2-year near 4.167% (+2bp) on Friday, against Federal Reserve H.15 constant maturities dated 13 August of 4.15% at 2 years, 4.63% at 10 years and 5.21% at 30 years - the H.15 values simply lag by a business day. The more telling datapoint remains that a 30-year auction cleared at 5.216%, the highest in 25 years, pointing to real long-end pressure alongside an otherwise calm equity tape.

Geopolitics remains the one live channel during the halt. The Strait of Hormuz is in roughly its 167th day of effective closure under a U.S. naval blockade; ship-tracking showed a single transit on 9 August against about 73 per day under normal conditions, and while eight to fifteen vessels crossed on 4-6 August, that is a fraction of the roughly 130 pre-conflict daily transits. Negotiations are deadlocked: Iran's foreign ministry states that while the blockade continues 'the necessary conditions for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz do not exist'. Treasury Secretary Bessent said the administration will apply measures 'like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation of a country', combined with continued blockade enforcement, and - importantly for timing - flagged the announcement for next week rather than for this weekend.

Interpretation: the signals genuinely conflict, which is why this is scored as elevated Stress with low Tail rather than as either calm or dangerous. Equity volatility pricing near 14 with a tight day range, index levels close to records, a mid-range orderly Friday close, a small-cap record and a third straight weekly gain argue against imminent pathological structure. A closed chokepoint on day 167, oil up about 5% on the week, a sharp consumer-demand and sentiment miss, a 25-year-high long-bond auction yield, a pending unprecedented sanctions package and a wobble in semiconductor leadership argue that the environment is difficult and gap-prone. Per the contract, conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail, and Stress must not decay to a trivial floor merely because the venue is shut while the catalyst set is unresolved - hence 45% here. Tail remains low at 9% because not one of the required Tail conditions - observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed pullbacks, repeated extension, NQ pinned near extremes - can be evidenced while no price is printing, and none was present at the last observable close.
lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 9-11% through the Asian and European sessions of Friday 14 August and easing to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session: the softer Retail Sales and University of Michigan prints and the Broadcom/Applied Materials drag produced two-way volatility and rotation into small caps, not directional efficiency. Stress described a clear event arc - roughly 23-29% in the quiet pre-dawn hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data and semiconductor news landed, then 34% after the 21:00 UTC weekly close and collapsing to 12% in the two post-close halt runs, before being corrected back to 45% at 00:00 UTC. That correction is the reading carried forward here: the venue shut, but the Hormuz closure, the oil rally and the pending sanctions package did not resolve, so the backdrop never justified a trivial weekend floor. Confidence trended down through Friday from the high 40s to the low 30s as supplementary data coverage degraded, recovered to the 50s once primary-source reads succeeded from 13:00 UTC, and sits at 57% for the most recent completed hour. The 20:00 UTC slot has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable. Every past hour is reproduced exactly as it was published and is not restated with later information.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it ends at 00:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, still roughly 22 hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is therefore projected flat at 9% for most of the window, ticking to 10% only in the final five slots as the reopen edges into view; this reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays in the low band so the action is EA_ON green throughout. Stress is projected to ease from 45% to about 41% through the thin Saturday Asian and European hours, when Gulf-related headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 44-45% into the late slots as unresolved weekend headlines converge on the Sunday gap; it stays inside the elevated band all horizon because the Hormuz closure, the oil rally, the consumer-demand miss and the pending Iran package are unresolved rather than because any event is scheduled. Confidence decays from 56% to 44% as Friday's verified evidence ages with nothing observable to replace it. The named danger window is the Sunday reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which sits just beyond this horizon; the next scheduled macro checkpoint is FOMC Minutes on 19 August at 18:00 UTC, with the Jackson Hole symposium falling on 27-29 August, outside the seven-day event window.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour sits deep inside the CME weekend halt: the last quote was Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing prints again until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August. Tail 9% reflects the total absence of an observable price path plus an orderly, mid-range Friday close; Stress 45% carries the unresolved Hormuz closure, the ~5% weekly oil rally and the pending U.S. Iran sanctions package.

Still fully halted through the Asian Saturday hours, historically the thinnest headline window of the week. No change in structure is possible, so Tail holds at 9% and Stress only begins to ease as the Gulf news cycle quiets.

Overnight Saturday. Stress edges to 44% because no new escalation has landed and the Bessent sanctions package is flagged for next week rather than this weekend; Tail unchanged at 9% with no venue quoting.
Pre-dawn Europe, halt continues. Confidence slips to 53% purely on the ageing of Friday's verified close, VIX and yield reads - there is nothing observable to refresh them with.

Saturday European morning. Stress 43% as the quiet-weekend drift continues; the oil rally and the 25-year-high 30-year auction yield remain unresolved backdrop rather than active catalysts, so Tail stays low at 9%.

Late Saturday morning. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere in this 24-hour horizon and no venue reopens inside it, so the action stays EA_ON green on Tail alone; the operative checkpoint is the Sunday reopen gap, which sits beyond this window.
